q: Suppose a person contains about 50 g of ATP at any moment but hydrolyses about 40 kg of ATP per day. What does this imply?
options: Each ATP is regenerated ~800 times a day, so ATP is a rapidly recycled carrier, not a store
About 40 kg of new adenine must be absorbed from food daily to replace the ATP that is used up
Extra ATP is stored in adipose tissue between meals and released when the 50 g pool runs low
Each ATP molecule lasts about 800 days before it is hydrolysed, so ATP is a long-term store
explanation: 40 000 g ÷ 50 g = 800, so each ATP molecule is hydrolysed to ADP + Pi and rephosphorylated about 800 times per day – roughly every 2 minutes. The adenosine part is recycled, not replaced. This huge turnover shows ATP is an immediate, short-term energy carrier that respiration must constantly regenerate; long-term storage uses glycogen and lipids.
